subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm/zswap: batch the writeback IO of consecutive entries

2026-10-07.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the writeback I/O of zswap by batching consecutive entries into a single bio, reducing the number of I/O requests and improving performance. The patch introduces a new struct to share state between all entries written back in one LRU walk, allowing for more efficient use of I/O resources. The changes are based on measurements that show significant improvements in build time, write requests, pages per write request, iocost debt, and IO full pressure when batching is enabled.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Nhat Pham noted that the improvement in batching writeback IO is limited because physical swap allocation may not be contiguous by the time of writeback due to refaults and holes, which could be mitigated by using vswap.

Gave Acked-by
reviews.raw_body:
The improvement is pretty big, but still only 1.3 :(

Is this because writeback entries are not contiguous in physical swap
space? Physical swap allocation algorithm has a bias for allocating
contiguous slots, but by writeback time we might have already punched
a bunch of holes (refaults etc.).

Ironically, vswap might help a bit here, because we defer physical
swap space allocation to right before writeback time... But who knows
:/

Anyway, I'll take the 20% :)

2026-10-09.patch_summary: This patch optimizes zswap writeback by batching consecutive entries into a single IO operation, reducing the number of write requests and improving performance. The patch introduces a new struct to share state between all entries written back by one LRU walk, allowing for more efficient use of swap cache and iocost throttling. The changes were tested with kernel build results showing significant improvements in writeback efficiency and reduced IO pressure.
